table_title: For each planet in the solar system, list its named moons that have a documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year (the Moon is listed as 'Prehistoric'), with their diameter in km, orbital period in days, and year of discovery.
db_analog: SELECT planet, moon, diameter_km, orbital_period_days, discovery_year FROM named_moons WHERE planet IN ('Mercury','Venus','Earth','Mars','Jupiter','Saturn','Uranus','Neptune') AND diameter_km IS NOT NULL AND orbital_period_days IS NOT NULL AND discovery_year IS NOT NULL ORDER BY planet, moon
temporal_note: Wikidata SPARQL endpoint snapshot, accessed 2026-04-28. The named-moon universe is the 137 IAU-named natural satellites of the eight solar-system planets that have all three of (diameter or mean radius), orbital period, and discovery date populated on Wikidata as of the snapshot. Mercury and Venus contribute zero rows because they have no natural satellites. Earth contributes one row (the Moon, Q405) and uses the literal string 'Prehistoric' in the Discovery Year column because human knowledge of the Moon predates recorded history and Wikidata records no P575 (time of discovery or invention) for it. Two sources of low-rate value drift: (a) IAU continues to name newly-discovered outer-planet satellites in batches (e.g., Jupiter and Saturn naming waves in 2018-2019 and 2024-2025), so the universe size will grow slowly; (b) numeric values for diameter and orbital period reflect the most recent published measurements and are occasionally revised on Wikidata. The relative ranking of major moons (Galilean, Titan, Triton, Miranda, etc.) is fixed.
_extraction_notes: Scope clarification (cycle-2 audit suggestion): the table_title's 'documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year' should be read as 'present in the cited Wikidata source set as of the snapshot date'. Several named moons that are documented in Wikipedia infoboxes or NASA fact sheets (e.g., Saturn's Pan, Atlas, Pandora, Prometheus) are excluded because Wikidata lacks both P2120 and P2386; this is a Wikidata-coverage limitation, not a claim about the underlying knowledge. Built via two-stage SPARQL extraction from datasets/build_benchmark/sparql_queries/planets_named_moons.sparql. Stage 1 fetches the named-moon universe per planet using the per-planet 'moon of X' classes (Q177268 Mars, Q61702557 Jupiter, Q1972 Saturn, Q2152 Uranus, Q2139 Neptune) plus an explicit Q405 Moon for Earth. Provisional designations are filtered out by two regex predicates: (1) labels starting with 'S/' (e.g., 'S/2003 J 24'), (2) labels of the form '<Planet> <Roman numeral>' (e.g., 'Uranus XXVIII') used as numbered placeholders for unnamed items. Stage 2 fetches mean radius (P2120) and diameter (P2386) and orbital period (P2146 with unit) and discovery date (P575) for each moon. Diameter precedence (cycle-2 audit fix): the post-processor PREFERS 2 * P2120 (mean radius doubled) over P2386 and uses P2386 only as fallback when P2120 is absent. The earlier cycle-0/cycle-1 pipeline used the inverse precedence and shipped at least one obvious data error (Juliet's P2386 = 936 km vs. true ~94 km / 2*P2120 = 106 km). The flipped precedence also matches Wikipedia's mean-diameter convention for triaxial bodies (e.g., Mimas now reports 396.4 km from radius doubling rather than 415.6 km long axis). Of 137 CSV rows, 62 use the 2*P2120 path and 75 use the P2386 fallback; per-planet split (radius / fallback): Earth 1/0, Mars 1/1 (Phobos via P2386), Jupiter 16/32, Saturn 15/35, Uranus 21/2 (Miranda and Sycorax via P2386), Neptune 8/5. Orbital periods are normalized to absolute days: Q573 (day) factor 1, Q577 (year) and Q1092296 (annum) factor 365.25. Negative orbital periods (which Wikidata uses to encode retrograde direction) are taken as |value|. Discovery dates are truncated to year and the minimum-year statement is used when multiple are present. When Wikidata has multiple values for a numeric attribute on the same item, the median is taken. Result: 137 rows x 5 columns, composite PK on (Planet, Moon), 0 duplicates. Per-planet row counts: Earth 1, Mars 2, Jupiter 48, Saturn 50, Uranus 23, Neptune 13 (unchanged from cycle 1; the precedence flip changed values but not row membership because every kept moon had at least one of P2120 or P2386). Per-planet drops (named moons present in Wikidata but missing both P2120 and P2386 and therefore excluded): Jupiter 9 (Metis, Adrastea, Thelxinoe, Euanthe, Hermippe, Ananke, Megaclite, Philophrosyne, Pandia), Saturn 14 (Pan, Atlas, Pandora, Prometheus, Suttungr, Gerd, Angrboda, Skrymir, Eggther, Themis, Gridr, Beli, Gunnlod, Thiazzi), Uranus 4 (Ophelia, Cordelia, Cressida, Bianca), Neptune 1 (Hippocamp); 0 drops for Earth or Mars.
